answer: Tie seats to a passport chip without exposing the holder. An operator taps an NFC passport; a zero-knowledge proof checks the issuing state's cipher signature and emits one nullifier per document, shared by at most 3 seats (assumed). Verifiers learn nothing else, so a holder from a tiny island nation stays as private as anyone. A 1,000-seat farm needs about 334 genuine passports (assumed). Forged chips must beat a government signature, so cover for fakes splits like shale.
